brand.note: Runtime brand colour from config/brand.ts (--brand). Raw only on non-text marks: rings, pager dot, caret.

brand-fill.note: color-mix(in srgb, var(--brand) 80%, #3a1d0f) — every text-bearing red fill; identical in dark mode.

brand-ink.note: color-mix(in srgb, var(--brand) 80%, #3a1d0f) — red as text on cream.

brand-soft.note: color-mix(in srgb, var(--brand) 12%, var(--ground)) — secondary button fill.

on-brand.note: Runtime --on-brand from config/brand.ts; text and rings on red.

accent.note: Runtime --accent from config/brand.ts; add, choose and notify signals.

on-accent.note: Runtime --on-accent; text on mustard and the ink-stroke colour.

ok.note: Trust icons, free fee, switch on, completed.

ink.note: Primary text and filled chip state.

ink-2.note: Secondary text, struck prices, field labels.

ground.note: Page, sheet and sticky footer background.

muted.note: Image wells, skeletons, hover, selected row.

bar-dark.note: Dark --bar, with an inset 2px cream top line.

display.purpose: Promo numeral and story-viewer title; uppercase shout, mustard with ink stroke on red.

headline.purpose: Page titles, home headline, onboarding, sheet product name (26–36px), uppercase shout.

item.purpose: Dish names and payment method names, sentence case.

body.purpose: Descriptions, greetings, hints; 17px on onboarding; inputs at 16px.

label.purpose: Buttons and text actions, uppercase (13/14/15px by size).

caption.purpose: Field labels (uppercase, ink-2), promise rows, story names, status chips.

price.purpose: Prices, counts and order ids in tabular figures; 16–32px by context.

shadows.name: none
shadows.purpose: The system has no elevation shadows; depth is a 2px outline and colour fill.

shadows.name: focus-ring-field
shadows.purpose: Zero-blur mustard ring on focused inputs; an outline, not elevation.

shadows.name: bar-top-line-dark
shadows.purpose: Dark mode only: 2px cream line along the bottom bar's top edge.

motion.name: ease-pop
motion.purpose: Expo ease-out for every transition and entrance; no overshoot.

motion.name: stamp
motion.purpose: Signature: quantity disc, cart badge and success check stamping in.

narrative.overview:
The app reads like the printed poster taped inside a loud neighbourhood burger joint, then lets you order from it. A warm cream ground carries white cards; every object is drawn with a fat 2px brown-ink outline and round, generous corners; offers are shouted in heavy uppercase Rubik; tomato red owns promotions, primary actions and new prices, and mustard marks the things you tap to add. It is appetite and fun first, but it is a working tool: prices are legible at a glance, the next action is always one thumb away, and the total is trusted before confirming.

Density is comfortable, not airy: a single 512px column, 16px gutters, two-up product cards, and stacked outlined panels. Depth comes from outline and colour, never from shadow; motion is quick expo ease-out where sheets rise and nothing bounces. The one memorable moment is the stamp: adding a dish presses a red quantity disc onto the card's corner like an ink stamp.

The system is a rebrandable template. Brand red, cream on-brand, mustard and brown on-accent are written to `<html>` at runtime from `frontend/src/config/brand.ts`; every red surface that carries text uses a fill darkened 20% toward ink so a restaurant's lighter brand colour still holds cream text. Confirmed rejections: the earlier "national ornament" ikat world (rejected by the user as "too traditional"), and the grey-card delivery-app default. All product photography currently shipped is an AI-generated placeholder (`frontend/public/images/products/*.jpg`) for each restaurant to replace.
keyCharacteristics: Cream ground, white cards, brown ink type and 2px brown outlines on everything.
Tomato red for promotions, primary CTAs and prices; mustard for add buttons, discount tags, active nav and toasts.
One typeface, Rubik Variable; weight does the hierarchy (900 shout, 800 labels, 500 body).
Pills and circles; no corner under 18px.
No shadows. Outline and colour fill are the only depth.
Signature: the quantity stamp disc, animated by the `stamp` keyframes.
Full Telegram dark theme: brown-black ground, cream ink, cream outlines.

rules.name: The Fired Fill Rule
rules.body: Any red area that carries text uses `brand-fill`, never raw `brand`. Raw brand is for rings, dots and carets only. This is what lets any restaurant's red pass with cream text; still check `onBrand` contrast when rebranding.

rules.name: The Mustard Means Add Rule
rules.body: Mustard marks what you touch to add, choose or be told: add buttons, the stepper plus, discount tags, the active tab, the selected payment method, the toast. Do not spend it on decoration.

rules.name: The Honest Price Rule
rules.body: The new price is Sale Red, 900, tabular; the old price is Toasted Crust, 500, struck through with a 1.5px line, set above it. A price never appears without the currency label beside it in `ink-2`.

rules.name: The Shout Rule
rules.body: Headings use the `shout` treatment: Rubik 900, uppercase, -0.025em, line-height 0.98, balanced wrapping. Dish names are the exception and stay sentence case at 800 so a two-line name stays readable.

rules.name: The Ink-Stroke Rule
rules.body: Mustard display numerals on red always carry a 4px Bun Brown stroke painted behind the fill (`-webkit-text-stroke` with `paint-order: stroke fill`). Mustard text never sits on red without it.

rules.name: The Tabular Price Rule
rules.body: Every number that is a price, count or order id uses tabular figures so columns and totals do not jitter.

rules.name: The Drawn Depth Rule
rules.body: If a layer needs to stand out, give it an outline or a different fill. A blurred shadow is never the answer, in either theme.

rules.name: The Fat Corner Rule
rules.body: No square corners and nothing under 18px. If it is interactive and small, it is a pill or a circle.

rules.name: The 2px Ink Rule
rules.body: Outlines and dividers are 2px in the outline colour. Not 1px, not grey.

dos: **Do** fill every text-bearing red surface with `brand-fill` and keep raw `brand` for rings, dots and the caret.
**Do** outline every card, chip, control, photo and divider in 2px of the outline colour.
**Do** set headings in the `shout` treatment (Rubik 900 uppercase, -0.025em, 0.98) and dish names in 800 sentence case.
**Do** give mustard numerals on red the 4px Bun Brown `ink-stroke`.
**Do** show prices as struck Toasted Crust old price over a Sale Red 900 tabular new price with the currency label.
**Do** use mustard for add, choose and confirm signals: "+" buttons, discount tags, active tab, selected payment, toast.
**Do** use Lucide icons at a 2.25 stroke, raising glyphs inside small filled controls to 2.5–3.

**Do** keep motion on the expo ease `cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1)`: sheets rise in 360ms, content rises 10px in 420ms, the stamp lands in 340ms, presses scale to 0.97 (pills) or 0.9 (round buttons); respect reduced motion.
**Do** fade only a disabled row's content (icon, text, radio) to 45%, leaving its divider and panel outline intact.
**Do** keep every brand-coloured value flowing from `brand.ts` so a restaurant can rebrand with four colours, and check `onBrand` contrast against the derived fill.
donts: **Don't** use drop shadows or blurred glows, in either theme; depth is outline and colour.
**Don't** put cream or white text on raw `brand`, or mustard text on red without the ink stroke.
**Don't** use square corners or radii under 18px on containers.
**Don't** draw 1px or grey outlines and dividers.
**Don't** bring back the rejected "national ornament" look: no ikat bands, abr silk patterns or traditional ornament.
**Don't** fall back to the grey-card delivery-app default: no grey surfaces, borderless floating cards or blue system accents.
**Don't** add a second typeface; hierarchy comes from Rubik's weights and the uppercase shout.
